pick.headline: Israel confirms it holds the nuclear whistle-blower Mordechai Vanunu
pick.summary: On 9 November 1986 the Israeli government announced that Mordechai Vanunu, a former technician at the Dimona nuclear centre who had given details of Israel's weapons programme to the Sunday Times, was in custody in Israel.
pick.significance: Vanunu had vanished from London weeks earlier; he had been lured to Rome by a Mossad agent and smuggled to Israel. His revelations exposed the scale of Israel's undeclared nuclear arsenal.
pick.fbis: FBIS's 10 November 1986 regional review reported, from IDF radio, the Israeli government secretariat's statement that Vanunu was being held in Israel under a court order, and its answer to rumours that he had been kidnapped.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: South Asia, Vol. VIII No. 217, 10 November 1986
evidence.snippet: …several “misled” military personnel have been arrested for disseminating clandes- tine circulars “inspired by the counterrevolution,” the Intei- ligence Ministry announced in a statement reported by Tehran radio. Israel Vanunu Affair — Mordekhay Vanunu is being detained in Israel in accordance with a court order, the government Secretariat announced in a statement reported by IDF radio 9 November. All rumors alleging that Vanunu was kidnapped…

alternates.headline: Gorbachev and Kohl sign a German-Soviet treaty in Bonn
alternates.summary: On 9 November 1990, a year to the day after the Berlin Wall opened, Mikhail Gorbachev and Helmut Kohl signed a treaty of good-neighbourliness, partnership and cooperation in Bonn.
alternates.significance: The treaty sealed the new relationship between Moscow and a united Germany, which was paying for the withdrawal of Soviet troops from the former GDR.
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union report of 9 November 1990 carried Moscow previews of Gorbachev's first visit to united Germany, at which he was expected to sign a treaty on good-neighbourly relations, partnership and cooperation.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Soviet Union, No. 218, 9 November 1990
evidence.snippet: …l significance is very high. This is Gorbachev’s first visit to the united Germany and first visit to Germany as president of the Soviet Union. Gorbachev is expected to sign a number of important agreements, including a treaty on goodneighbourly rela- tions, partnership and cooperation. These agreements will lay the foundation for large-scale cooperation between the two countries in the spheres of economy, industry, science and technology. Ge…
